metadata.title: Eric Hernandez vs Justin Schieber: Does God Exist?
metadata.label: Evil, mind, and hiddenness
metadata.motion: Does theism or atheistic naturalism better explain evil, objective morality, knowledge, rationality, consciousness, free will, animal suffering, cosmic hostility, and non-resistant nonbelief?
metadata.sourceNote: Assessment based exclusively on the complete locally cached YouTube caption transcript and timestamped events (transcript SHA-256 c1aae59e4251c4458d4a8a1c1229868e90d84a4981d96156c5b925adee3f247b). Required below-high-confidence audio checks were completed before adjudication; representative quotations must be exact strings from quote-eligible locked source spans.
metadata.scoringNote: Scores are AI-generated estimates of argumentative performance under the locked adjudicated-consensus workflow. Repository code calculated every move, section, and overall result once, only after two isolated judgments, required audio review, and disputed-field adjudication closed.

routes.description: Establish Christian theism as the better explanation by connecting objective morality, trustworthy rational agency, consciousness, and freedom to a divine personal ground while showing that theism can accommodate the evidential challenges from suffering, cosmic conditions, and nonbelief.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if its positive divine-grounding account jointly explains the principal mental, moral, and epistemic phenomena and its auxiliary theological explanations make the principal naturalistic evidence insufficient to overturn that comparative case.

motionBridge.description: Show that Christian theism provides the more unified and adequate explanation of the motion's moral, epistemic, mental, agential, and evidential phenomena.

centralBridges.description: Connect objective moral truth, obligation, and the intelligibility of evil to a necessary personal transcendent ground.
Explain reliable cognition, rational inference, responsibility, and meaningful freedom through purposive agency rather than unguided adaptive causation alone.
Account for irreducible finite consciousness through an ultimate divine consciousness and an immaterial dimension of persons.
Supply theistically coherent reasons why animal suffering, cosmic hostility, and nonresistant nonbelief may occur despite divine goodness and love.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Test whether naturalistic additions for morality and consciousness preserve the simplicity and unity claimed for that worldview.
Relate fine-tuning, cosmic habitability conditions, restoration, soul-building, and divine hiddenness to the broader purposive account.

routes.description: Establish atheistic naturalism as the better explanation by combining its comparative simplicity with naturalistic accounts of morality, cognition, consciousness, and freedom, while treating animal suffering, cosmic hostility, and nonresistant nonbelief as evidence more expected without a perfectly good and loving creator.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if naturalism accommodates the positive phenomena without requiring a divine ground and if the observed patterns of suffering, cosmic inhospitability, and sincere nonbelief remain materially more congruent with indifferent natural processes than with Christian theism.

motionBridge.description: Show that atheistic naturalism explains the full evidential pattern with fewer fundamental commitments and without the tensions generated by a perfect divine creator.

centralBridges.description: Provide naturalistic resources for objective morality, reliable cognition, irreducible consciousness, reasons-responsive freedom, and rational agency.
Show why the scale, history, and predatory organization of nonmoral animal suffering are expected under indifferent evolution but require substantive explanation under theism.
Connect cosmic hostility and the distribution of nonresistant nonbelief to naturalistic expectations while identifying their tension with divine purpose and perfect love.
Test whether appeals to the fall, freedom, soul-building, compensation, hiddenness, and divine moral grounding explain the specific phenomena rather than merely permitting them.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Apply qualitative simplicity while allowing evidentially motivated fundamental phenomenal or normative features within naturalism.
Examine the compatibility of Molinism with libertarian freedom and the objectivity of morality grounded in a divine person.

sections.title: Objective Morality, Divine Grounding, and Evil
sections.rationale: This issue tests whether moral truth, authority, teleology, and the classification of evil require a necessary personal ground or can exist as irreducible normative facts without God.

sections.title: Knowledge, Rationality, and Evolutionary Determination
sections.rationale: The comparative case depends on whether unguided evolution and causal determination undermine trustworthy cognition or can generate reliable, content-sensitive, reasons-responsive belief formation.

sections.title: Consciousness, Freedom, and Explanatory Simplicity
sections.rationale: This section addresses whether irreducible consciousness and meaningful agency require souls and an ultimate mind, or fit a naturalistic account with fundamental phenomenal properties and compatibilist freedom.

sections.title: Animal Suffering, Predation, and Theodicy
sections.rationale: The long history and organized forms of nonmoral suffering create a major comparative test between indifferent evolution and theistic explanations involving freedom, the fall, soul-building, restoration, or compensation.

sections.title: Cosmic Hostility, Fine-Tuning, and Habitability
sections.rationale: The universe's limited hospitality to embodied moral life must be weighed against fine-tuning, the functional role of cosmic scale and emptiness, and competing expectations about divine creative purpose.

sections.title: Nonresistant Nonbelief and Perfect Divine Love
sections.rationale: The existence and distribution of sincere nonbelief test whether perfect love requires accessible relationship with God or permits hiddenness for protective, developmental, or relational purposes.
